channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Trump says US has not agreed to Ukraine producing Patriot missiles
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Friday that Washington had not agreed to allow Ukraine to produce Patriot missiles, contradicting remarks by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky following talks between the two leaders earlier this week.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Hamas agrees to disarm under Trump ceasefire deal
item.description: Hamas said on Friday it had agreed to hand over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee as part of a US-backed roadmap that would see a gradual Israeli military withdrawal from Gaza, though Israel said it would not pull back until the militant group is fully disarmed.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: George Clooney's family evacuates their home in France amid wildfires
item.description: George Clooney and his family have evacuated their home in southeastern France after a nearby wildfire threatened the area, his agent said Thursday. Blazes continued to scorch parts of the country during a prolonged spell of extreme summer heat.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Strong El Nino 'adding fuel to a planet already on fire', warns UN chief
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned on Friday that a strengthening El Niño is intensifying an already worsening climate crisis, saying the weather phenomenon is "adding fuel to a planet already on fire" and could drive record-breaking global temperatures.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Trump blames Spain for migrant chaos despite return of tens of thousands to Morocco
item.description: US President Donald Trump and other far-right leaders on Friday seized on Spain's migration crisis to bolster their political messaging on immigration, while over half of the migrants who had crossed the border made their way back to Morocco voluntarily the same day.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Replay: US President Donald Trump addresses Cabinet meeting
item.description: Rewatch US President Donald Trump's address during a cabinet meeting at the Camp David retreat following the announcement that Hamas had agreed to disarm in Gaza as part of a US-brokered plan.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Donald Trump trying to 'change the narrative away from the Iran war' ahead of midterms
item.description: US President Donald Trump held a cabinet meeting at the Camp David retreat where he addressed a wide range of subjects, from Iran to the midterm elections. He also blamed the Spanish government for the mass migrant arrivals in Spain's Ceuta enclave, calling it an invasion. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson was listening to the president's address and tells us what to know.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Hamas disarming would be 'first concrete step to re-energise peace plan', but questions remain
item.description: Israel will not withdraw from the Gaza Strip until Hamas's "genuine disarmament", a political source told AFP on July 31, after the group said it had agreed to a deal involving its disarmament and Israel's exit. But officially, the country has stayed silent regarding the agreement. It was announced by US President Donald Trump and could represent the 'first step forward' since the ceasefire in Gaza, says FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Gaza Strip: Will Hamas really disarm?
item.description:
🇮🇱 🇵🇸 Hamas confirmed Friday it had agreed to a deal with #Israel that would lead to the group's disarmament.
🇺🇸 This was a condition of the second phase of a #Gaza peace plan brokered by #US President Donald #Trump.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'The #Odyssey': What's missing from #Nolan's film according to Homer's translator
item.description: Since Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" came out, it has generated over $300 million… and a growing conversation about what is missing compared to the original poem. But what is that exactly? In a scathing review published recently, classicist and translator of Homer’s epic, Emily Wilson, had much to say about what differed from the original poem. Her translation, published in 2017, was widely acclaimed, and Nolan said she was one of the inspirations for his film in early publicity. FRANCE 24 spoke to her a few days before she published her review, and here’s what she had to say.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Why did Riyadh join US strikes on Tehran's allies in Iraq?
item.description: Saudi Arabia joined the United States for the first time in launching air strikes against Iran-backed militias in Iraq on Wednesday, marking a significant shift in the kingdom's regional posture after months of restraint. While Riyadh insists it was acting in self-defence, the operation raises questions about whether the kingdom is abandoning its cautious approach towards Tehran – or simply sending a warning.
item.dc:creator: Sébastian SEIBT

item.title: Greece orders partial evacuation of Athens suburb as wildfire burns
item.description: Greek authorities on Friday ordered the partial evacuation of a suburb west of Athens after a forest fire broke out on a nearby mountain, prompting an emergency alert as firefighters battled to contain the blaze.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Although France's mega fire has eased, the dangers firefighters face haven't
item.description: Firefighters in southwestern France were working to control the last hot spots of a massive wildfire that has burned an area four times the size of Paris and forced thousands out of their homes. The blazes that have burned 42,000 hectares of pine forest and touristic areas in Bordeaux's Gironde region haven't spread for several days, and officials are cautiously optimistic. But for those on the frontline, the danger hasn't eased. Officials say more than 230 firefighters have been injured, and the toll keeps rising the longer they stay on the line.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Heatwave pushes energy-hungry Tunisia to enforce rolling blackouts
item.description: In Tunisia, after weeks of extended power cuts, the effects are serious. Between 150 and 200 died in the heatwave, according to the Order of Young Doctors, and businesses took severe hits after their goods spoiled. Authorities have announced that power is returning to normal as temperatures go back down this week. This crisis has highlighted Tunisia’s fragile dependence on energy as climate change sees regularly higher temperatures. FRANCE 24's Lilia Blaise and Hamdi Tlili report.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Cameroon president's absence sparks debate over government inaction
item.description: The lengthy absence of Cameroon's long-serving President Paul Biya, who has been in Switzerland since early June, has reignited debate about government inaction, in a country where many crave change. Biya has made frequent trips to Geneva over the years and has faced waves of speculation and rumours regarding his health. FRANCE 24's Indira Ayuk tells us more from Yaoundé.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: More than 48,000 migrants return to Morocco after thousands cross border into Spain
item.description: Spain said on Friday it had largely reversed a surge of migrants into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with 48,000 of the people who crossed from Morocco by land and sea already returning voluntarily.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: No, this video does not show a drone attack on ships in Egypt
item.description: Following reports of a drone attack on a US-owned gas storage vessel at Egypt’s Damietta port, a video purporting to show the incident began circulating online. The footage, however, is unrelated to the conflict in the Middle East. FRANCE 24 found that the footage instead shows a Ukrainian drone striking a Russian ship in the Black Sea.
item.dc:creator: Ershad ALIJANI

item.title: In Naples, archaeologists work to learn more about a submerged Roman city
item.description: About 30 kilometres to the west of Naples lies one of the Roman Empire's most prestigious coastal thermal resorts. It gradually sank below sea level over time due to subsidence caused by the volcanic nature of the region. Today, it continues to reveal new secrets. To better understand and preserve this exceptional heritage, the universities of Naples and Salerno, with the participation of several private companies, are developing new technology as part of a research programme.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: If it disarms, Hamas would 'take away Israel's rationale' to occupy Gaza
item.description: Hamas said on July 31 it agreed to a deal to end the war with Israel that included provisions addressing its weapons and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip. US President Donald Trump announced the plan, calling it a critical step towards a new Palestinian government in Gaza. But what would that mean for the region, is it all that simple and why is it coming now? FRANCE 24's Matthew-Mary Caruchet tells us more.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Spain's PM blames trafficking mafia for ongoing Ceuta migrant crisis
item.description: Spain's Pedro Sanchez criticised a sudden arrival of around 40,000 migrants from Morocco to the north African enclave Ceuta as "an attack, a violation" of Spain's national territory. The prime minister blamed the influx of immigrants on criminal networks manipulating a recent court ruling that immediate returns of migrants crossing the border illegally did not apply to those arriving by sea. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris tells us more
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: France’s wildfires: Famous Bordeaux wine region at risk
item.description:
🇫🇷 🍷 #France's largest #wine region is facing a wake-up call after #wildfires neared #Bordeaux's famed vineyards.
The blazes underscored the climate challenges posed by severe drought and repeated #heatwaves.
FRANCE 24's Gabrielle Nadler explains ▶️
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Infantino's senior advisor resigns amid outrage over FIFA's private investment plan
item.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino's senior advisor has resigned in protest over his boss's plan to seek private investment for the World Cup football tournament. Carlos Cordeiro said such a move would "mortgage football's future."His voice part of a growing opposition - which includes a potential boycott by Europe's football associations - as well as CONCACAF - the governing body for football in North and Central America and the Asian Football confederation. FIFA is currently offering 40 million dollars to each country that backs its project.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: What to know about the arrival of 49,000 migrants into Spain's Ceuta
item.description: In the span of 24 hours, Spanish authorities estimate that over 49,000 migrants crossed in Spain from Morocco, with at least 18 dying as they tried to reach the enclave of Ceuta. The migrants crossed the border by swimming across, sometimes spending hours in the water. The arrivals are way over half the population of the enclave. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris tells us more from Spain.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
